headline: Man faces attempted-murder charges after Bridgewater State students hit by car
dek: A driver is accused of intentionally steering into two students during Homecoming weekend; one suffered serious but non-life-threatening injuries, according to university officials.
body: Two Bridgewater State University students were injured Saturday morning after a driver is accused of steering a vehicle into them on campus during the university's Homecoming weekend. The university said the collision happened on Burrill Avenue near the Moakley Center, where one student suffered serious but non-life-threatening injuries and was taken to a hospital. A second student had minor injuries. The students' names had not been released in the reports reviewed Monday.

Boston 25 News reported that the incident occurred while an estimated 10,000 people were on campus for Homecoming activities. University officials said surveillance video captured the event and indicated that the driver acted intentionally. That account describes the central allegation in the case; it is not a court finding, and the circumstances remain under investigation.

Bridgewater State President Frederick W. Clark Jr. told students and staff that the driver, described as a man in his early 40s from East Weymouth, has no affiliation with the university. Bridgewater State police arrested him near the Moakley Center and took him for a psychiatric evaluation, according to the university statement cited by [CBS Boston](https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/bridgewater-state-students-injured-hit-by-car/). Officials had not publicly released his name as of Monday.

The charges listed by university officials are two counts of attempted murder, two counts of reckless operation of a motor vehicle, leaving the scene of personal injury and a marked-lanes violation. The allegations have not been tested at trial. CBS Boston reported that the driver had allegedly been involved in an earlier road-rage incident in East Bridgewater. The university said investigators had no evidence that the two students were specifically targeted, even though the act of striking them appeared deliberate.

The episode was especially disruptive because it unfolded during a major campus gathering. Bridgewater State's [official Homecoming schedule](https://www.bridgew.edu/homecoming/schedule-of-events) shows tailgating, a block party, athletic events and other activities were planned for Saturday, Oct. 3. Boston 25 said the collision took place near the Moakley Center during that weekend program. The combination of a crowded event and a vehicle moving toward students made the incident a significant safety concern for the university community, although the public reports do not describe any broader threat to campus.

The university police department is leading the investigation with help from an accident-reconstruction team and Bridgewater police, according to [Boston 25 News](https://cmg-cmg-tv-10020-prod.cdn.arcpublishing.com/news/local/driver-charged-with-attempted-murder-after-striking-2-bsu-students-during-homecoming-weekend/DHQMEQOEENGCPCVDOSPLLUQMFY/). The next confirmed developments are expected to come from investigators or the court system, including the driver's identity, arraignment information, the students' recovery and a fuller account of what preceded the collision. None of those details had been reported by the time of publication.

Bridgewater State says its [police department](https://www.bridgew.edu/about-us/police-department) protects students, employees and visitors and has authority on university property and throughout the town. The department's published information lists patrol, detective, prosecution and emergency-medical functions, as well as regional law-enforcement partnerships. That structure helps explain why the case involves campus police and municipal investigators, but it does not resolve the evidence or the charges against the driver.

The university said it remained in contact with the hospitalized student's family and was supporting both students' families. For now, the verified facts are limited to the injuries, arrest, charges and investigative steps described by the university and independently reported by Boston 25 and CBS Boston. The motive, the driver's medical status, and any eventual court outcome remain unknown.
author: NorthEast News Desk
